actual: SD-29 was closed prematurely with three lanes unfinished. Five cards had work that was NEVER DISPATCHED, not attempted-and-blocked: epic-5-monster-lane-extend (ingest), epic-6-race-trait-lane-pilot (ingest), epic-6-race-trait-lane-extend (ingest), epic-7-companion-lane-pilot (entire card), epic-7-companion-lane-extend (entire card). Operator ruled this SD-29 scope and REOPENED the bundle: 'this is part of sd-29 scope. sd-29 is not done. lets get after it.' Mechanism of the error: kanban.md DECISION-BLOCKED legend ('terminal state, not a wait') was applied to cards where only one half had been delivered, so the undelivered ingest half silently inherited the delivered chassis/classifier half's terminal status

actual: Those are TOTALS, not remaining, and one was simply wrong. True: monster 1,270 total / 60 grounded / 1,210 remaining (card 8's 1,224 was wrong outright); race_trait 3,447 total / 21 grounded / 3,426 remaining; companion 1,696 total / 0 grounded / 1,696 remaining (card 12's 1,683 predates the Epic 6 companion mis-classification fix that ADDED 13 units); monster_ability 3,107 total / 17 grounded / 3,090 remaining. Only companion coincides as total-and-remaining, and only because zero companion units are grounded. The brief's own stated worry (double-counting across books / missed kind nesting) did NOT materialise; the real defect was total-vs-remaining conflation
